candidates.name: Stargardt disease
support_spans: symmetric hypoautofluorescent lesions with hyperautofluorescent borders in the central macula bilaterally
thinning of the outer nuclear layer in the fovea, partial preservation of the ellipsoid zone
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging results, including fundus autofluorescence and optical coherence tomography, are consistent with Stargardt disease, a common form of juvenile macular degeneration.

candidates.name: Cone-rod dystrophy
support_spans: attenuated photopic responses and 30-Hz flicker responses with delayed implicit times in both eyes
non-recordable photopic and 30-Hz flicker responses in both eyes
candidates.why: The electroretinography results showing impaired photopic responses and delayed implicit times support a diagnosis of cone-rod dystrophy, which affects the cone cells in the retina first and then the rod cells.

candidates.name: Macular dystrophy
support_spans: central scotoma in both eyes
macular atrophy and lesions bilaterally
candidates.why: The presence of central scotomas, macular atrophy, and lesions in both eyes suggests a diagnosis of macular dystrophy, a group of inherited disorders that affect the macula and cause progressive vision loss.

macular atrophy and lesions bilaterally
candidates.why: The father's symptoms of progressive blurred central vision and color vision defects, along with the electroretinography and fundus examination findings, could be indicative of retinitis pigmentosa.

candidates.name: Retinitis pigmentosa

selector.rationale: Cone-rod dystrophy best explains the combination of attenuated photopic responses, delayed implicit times, and structural changes like loss of the ellipsoid zone and collapse of the outer nuclear layer in the central macula bilaterally, without contradiction.

rejected.label: Retinitis pigmentosa

rejected.label: Macular dystrophy
